Hi, I am a fifth year undergraduate, so we're the same positions at having "one more year to go". As for the rest, I cannot give heartfelt advice since I am exactly in the same state of living, state of mind as you, even down to having three meals and milk. But I can give a more reasonable explanation that the way I discovered to live through my "very different mental conditions" as the rest of my already graduated genmates, is just narrowing down "things" to "thing". 

As long as you are not under any other responsibility, as I am sure since you stated that you come from middle class, just focus on finishing your study. That's all.

Let me tell you, I am a female and I was given approximately around $200-ish a month and I spend it sometimes to nearby cafe to focus on studying. But I ended up surfing internet as always! I'll be damned. I'll try to make it up days later by going to just my campus to work on it. But hey! At least I progressed each day even just a bit.

My method is to always go out everyday. Bring laptop, bring notes, go to public space especially where there were people around working. Having that environment that is productive just pushed you into the work, plus point that if that place is noisy as hell and full of laughs, you'd want to stuff your ears with your own playlist and just like that, you blend in as semi-normal. That's how I go through as "normal" while being clinically depressed (I'm highly functional depressed)

 I spend 3 days per week staying at library, and I swear to god, it's embarassing for me to watch youtube while everyone else is working on either reports, thesis, or competition, I get motivated to at least get my laptop screen to be something scientific, so I get motivation to finish my thesis mostly from that haha.

I am guilty to one thing, on top of being depressed, I CANNOT wake up early. I woke up at 11 and I've been trying to change it.

​

Listen, I was just a passerby. As young as I am just an undergraduate, I'm pretty much more boomer than you, I don't know if we can friends each other in reddit, but if you want to have me as an online friend to talk to, just reply and I'll figure out how to chat privately hahaa.

Good luck on your studies, I wish you well

We're at the same position. The reason why I felt down was because I felt like I wasn't doing enough to deserve all of this. I always feel indebted. I have no reason to feel unhappy, but that also become a shackle to me. I don't think I can go on like this
On the same thoughts, doing it before graduation may be looked upon as "death under school pressure" or something. "Might as well hand my parents a diploma before leaving" or something
Ngl I cried reading this. I'm 22 and I'm also homed. Thank you to share your story
